corridor: Oceanside Harbor to Border Field, San Diego County, CA

_moved.2.0.0: 2.0.0 REMOVES tidepool_floor_ft, tidepool_floor_confidence and the 8 floor_evidence ledgers. They are in shared/intertidal.json as floor_ft, floor_confidence and floor_evidence under membership.members, with that file's _provenance header stating the derivation and the commit they came from. Major, not minor: any reader of the three fields breaks, and two of them are Python. This file is bindings and joins -- values resolved by join against an upstream authority, never hand-populated -- which is what its _schema has always claimed and what the floor never was. See docs/adr/0002-measured-zone-facts-are-a-third-provenance-class.md. Note that this file's own unresolved array still carries the floor caveats, including the entry marked SAFETY: they are rendered verbatim from here today and moving them is #132, not this change.
_moved.3.0.0: 3.0.0 REMOVES audiences. It was a hand-populated tag in a file whose own rule forbids hand-populated values, and it had already duplicated a membership axis in silence: audiences:tidepool and a non-null tidepool_floor_ft were the same 8 spots exactly, with nothing checking it. Membership is a zone property now (shared/intertidal.json), and bird and sail are not activities this stack computes -- their spots stay, only the tag goes. Major, not minor: any reader of the field breaks. WHAT DID NOT GO WITH IT is the scope of the county_station join, which the tag carried: that is county_station_scope now, machine-readable where the predicate was prose. See docs/adr/0011-a-join-carries-its-own-scope.md.

conventions.coordinate_precision: ~100 m; suitable for station assignment, not navigation

mpa.publisher: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
mpa.disclaimer: This dataset is not intended for navigational use or defining legal boundaries.
mpa.dates: TWO DATES, FIVE YEARS APART, and neither on its own is 'the pull date'. content_date is what the layer's own description states its data are -- California's MPAs 'as January 1, 2019'. layer_last_edit_date is editingInfo.lastEditDate on the service. Recording one and calling it the layer's age misrepresents it in whichever direction was picked, so both are committed and tools/mpa/rejoin.py checks both. Consequence worth stating: a 2023-26 petition proposing boundary changes at Swami's could not be reflected in a 2019 snapshot. The join is not wrong; it is a dated snapshot that did not say so before 3.1.0.

_schema.slug: Stable primary key. Never change after first write; data accumulates against it.
_schema.name: Display name. Safe to change.
_schema.wave.primary: Buoy actually queried today. NDBC WMO id, or null for non-wave sites.
_schema.wave.fallback: Used when primary is not delivering. May be geographically distant; UI must disclose substitution.
_schema.wave.intended_primary: Buoy that SHOULD serve this spot but is currently dead. Reassign here when the REVIVED tripwire fires.
_schema.county_station: State/county beach water quality monitoring station code (e.g. OC-080) from the data.ca.gov Beach Water Quality Monitoring Stations resource. Resolved by nearest-neighbour against Active, located, individually-named stations only, over the spots county_station_scope marks 'in'. null means unresolved OR out of join scope -- read county_station_scope to tell which, and county_station_null_reason for why. Must never render as a pass. Re-runnable and diffable: tools/county-station/rejoin.py.
_schema.county_station_distance_m: Great-circle metres from the spot to its matched station; null when there is no match. Replaces the 1.0.0 field county_station_distance_km.
_schema.county_station_suspect: true when the match exceeds 1000 m, meaning the station may sit on a different beach cell carrying different water. The UI must disclose a suspect match rather than render it as a clean reading. null when there is no match.
_schema.county_station_null_reason: Present only when county_station is null, and required whenever it is. States why the field is empty: out of join scope, or genuinely unresolved. A null county_station without this key is a bug.
_schema.county_station_scope: Whether this spot is IN the county_station join's scope. 'in' means the join covers it, so a null station there is genuinely unresolved. 'out' means the join deliberately does not cover it and the null is not a gap; county_station_null_reason says why. Required on every spot, so one added later cannot be silently un-scoped -- scripts/gen-spots-types.mjs fails without it. THIS IS AN INPUT TO THE JOIN, NOT A RESULT OF IT, which is why it is written by hand in a file whose rule forbids hand-populated values: that rule governs what an upstream authority resolves, and no authority can state which spots this repo chose to ask about. HISTORY: up to 2.x the scope was the sentence 'ONLY for spots tagged swim, surf, dive or tidepool' in this schema, evaluated against the audiences field. 3.0.0 deleted that field, and the predicate is kept here as the historical scope that PRODUCED this set rather than as a rule to re-evaluate -- three of its four terms name activities this stack does not compute, and inventing referents for them would be worse than recording what was done. The set is unchanged by the deletion: 23 in, 3 out, exactly the split county_station_null_reason already carried.
_schema.mpa: Marine protected area NAME from CDFW ds582, resolved by point-in-polygon. null means the point fell outside every MPA polygon. Do not hand-populate. Read together with mpa_resolved: a null with mpa_resolved false is unknown, not unprotected. Re-runnable and diffable: tools/mpa/rejoin.py. The layer this resolved against, and its two dates, are joins.mpa.
_schema.mpa_resolved: true once the CDFW point-in-polygon join has run AND the result survives this file's ~100 m coordinate precision. false where the spot lies within 150 m of an MPA boundary, i.e. inside the coordinate error bar, so the in/out call is not trustworthy either way. Legally load-bearing wherever collection rules are presented, which today means the intertidal: shared/intertidal.json's members are the spots a reader may be standing on a reef at.
_schema.mpa_type: CDFW ds582 Type for the area named in mpa: SMR, SMCA, or SMCA (No-Take). A JOIN RESULT, and deliberately NOT derived from the name -- every corridor area's name happens to end in its type ('Cabrillo SMR'), so string-matching would work today and would be hand-populating a legally load-bearing field in a different costume. This is what decides whether take is permitted: an SMR and an SMCA (No-Take) prohibit take of any kind, an SMCA permits specified take. The corridor holds 3 SMRs, 5 SMCAs and 3 SMCA (No-Take), so a renderer that treats every resolved area as a reserve is wrong about 8 of the 11. null exactly when mpa is null; scripts/gen-spots-types.mjs fails on any other pairing. The value set is joins.mpa.types_published, asserted against the live service by the re-join.
_schema.ccr_section: The 14 CCR section 632(b) subsection number for the area named in mpa, from ds582 CCR_Int -- 138 Swami's SMCA, 143 South La Jolla SMR, 146 Cabrillo SMR. It is the join key back to ds582 and to the published vertex tables, the identifier a warden cites, and the stable id if a name ever changes. CDFW publishes the same subsection twice, as the integer CCR_Int and as the string CCR ('Section 632 (b) (146)'); the integer is committed because the string is a presentation of it, and one fact in two fields of one file is what this file's own _moved entries exist to undo. tools/mpa/rejoin.py asserts the two agree upstream rather than assuming it. null exactly when mpa is null.
_schema.joins: Per-join record of the upstream layer a join result came from: what was read, from where, when, and which version of it. A join result whose access path is unrecorded cannot be re-run or audited, which is the one thing this file's rule requires of one -- and the mpa join was in exactly that state until 3.1.0, with four sentences of prose naming ds582 and not one URL anywhere in the repo. ONLY mpa IS RECORDED HERE TODAY. county_station's provenance is the pinned constants in tools/county-station/rejoin.py and has not been lifted into this block, because inventing a retrieval date for a pull nobody dated would be worse than the gap. The asymmetry is recorded rather than tidied away.

46235.name: Imperial Beach Nearshore
46235.note: Station page serves 200 while realtime2 404s. Six south-corridor spots fall back to 46232 across ~15 mi of differing exposure. Reassign on REVIVED.

spots.name: Oceanside Harbor
spots.notes: Harbor mouth; sailing departure point. Watch PZZ740 for small craft advisories.

spots.name: Oceanside Pier
spots.notes: San Luis Rey outfall is just north; USGS 11042000 is the relevant discharge signal after rain.

spots.name: Buccaneer Beach
spots.notes: Loma Alta Creek outlet; chronic dry-weather bacteria site. County station join matters here.

spots.name: Tamarack State Beach
spots.notes: Agua Hedionda lagoon mouth immediately north.

spots.name: Batiquitos Lagoon
spots.notes: No wave binding. Tide still drives mudflat exposure and shorebird foraging; keep tide_station populated.

spots.name: Beacon's Beach
spots.notes: Bluff access; trail condition is a real hazard independent of surf.

spots.name: Moonlight State Beach
spots.notes: Cottonwood Creek outlet; lifeguarded, family default for Encinitas.

spots.name: Swami's
spots.notes: Reef point. MPA UNRESOLVED: point-in-polygon puts this 18 m OUTSIDE Swami's SMCA, far inside this file's ~100 m coordinate precision, so neither in nor out can be asserted. Do not present collection rules from the mpa field until the coordinate is surveyed.

spots.name: Cardiff Reef
spots.notes: San Elijo lagoon mouth adjacent; post-rain water quality degrades quickly.

spots.name: San Elijo Lagoon
spots.notes: Ecological reserve. High eBird hotspot density.

spots.name: Torrey Pines State Beach
spots.notes: Los Penasquitos lagoon mouth. Long beach; a single point is a poor proxy for its full length.

spots.name: Black's Beach
spots.notes: Scripps submarine canyon focuses swell; this spot breaks materially larger than neighbours on the same buoy reading. Threshold offsets needed.

spots.name: La Jolla Shores
spots.notes: Primary shore-dive entry for the corridor. Dike Rock tidepools at the north end. MPA UNRESOLVED: 45 m outside Matlahuayl SMR, inside the ~100 m coordinate error bar. The earlier expectation of San Diego-Scripps Coastal SMCA was simply wrong -- that boundary is 1003 m away. The open question here is Matlahuayl, not Scripps.

spots.name: La Jolla Cove
spots.notes: MPA UNRESOLVED: 21 m outside Matlahuayl SMR, inside the ~100 m coordinate error bar, so no-take status cannot be asserted either way. Matlahuayl is no take of any kind if the point resolves inside, so treat it as restricted until surveyed. Pinniped closures apply seasonally and are not in any API.

spots.name: Windansea
spots.notes: Reef break, rock hazard on low tide.

spots.name: Tourmaline Surf Park
spots.notes: Longboard and beginner-friendly; surf threshold should skew lower than neighbours.

spots.name: Mission Beach
spots.notes: Highest general-beachgoer volume in the corridor. Rip current statements matter most here.

spots.name: Ocean Beach Pier
spots.notes: San Diego River mouth immediately north; post-rain plume site.

spots.name: Sunset Cliffs
spots.notes: SAFETY: ledge system with cliff access. Getting the tidepool floor wrong here strands people. Verify before shipping.

spots.name: Cabrillo Tidepools
spots.notes: National Monument: gate hours and entry fee constrain access independently of tide. Point-in-polygon puts this INSIDE Cabrillo SMR -- an SMR, not the SMCA previously assumed, so no take of any kind -- but by only 11 m, inside the ~100 m coordinate error bar, hence mpa_resolved false. The thin margin is a reason to verify the boundary, never to relax the restriction. Best-known tidepool site in the corridor.

spots.name: Coronado Central Beach
spots.notes: Increasingly affected by south-county transboundary flows. Least Tern nesting closures seasonally.

spots.name: Silver Strand State Beach
spots.notes: Ocean side uses 9410230. If a bayside spot is added later it must use 9410170; do not reuse this record.

spots.name: Imperial Beach Pier
spots.notes: Most closure-affected spot in the corridor. IBWC station 11013300 is the upstream flow signal, but dry-weather canyon collectors enter downstream of that gauge: a low reading does NOT imply clean water here.

spots.name: Border Field State Park
spots.notes: Tijuana River estuary. MPA UNRESOLVED: 3 m outside Tijuana River Mouth SMCA -- effectively on the line and far inside the ~100 m coordinate error bar. Frequently under long-duration closure; water contact audiences should be suppressed, not shown as poor.

unresolved: county_station is resolved on 23 of 26 spots. The nearest-neighbour join covers the spots county_station_scope marks 'in'; the other 3 (batiquitos-lagoon, san-elijo-lagoon, border-field) are marked 'out' and carry null plus county_station_null_reason. Up to 2.x the scope was 'spots tagged swim, surf, dive or tidepool' read off the audiences field, which 3.0.0 deleted; the set is identical either way, and tools/county-station/rejoin.py re-runs the join and diffs it against these values. The source resource needs filtering before use as a point set: of 287 San Diego records only 123 are Active, 12 have no coordinates, and All_SanDiego_County_Beaches and Northern_SanDiego_County_Beaches are county-wide aggregates holding one coordinate near San Onofre. Pool: 121.

1 in-scope match exceeds 1000 m and is flagged county_station_suspect: beacons-leucadia at 1402 m. Beacon's sits in a real ~4 km monitoring gap between EH-440 and EH-420A, so no closer station exists to find.

mpa point-in-polygon has run against CDFW ds582 for all 26 spots, but 7 carry mpa_resolved false: the spot lies within 150 m of an MPA boundary, inside this file's own ~100 m coordinate precision, so the in/out call cannot be trusted either way (moonlight-encinitas, swamis, cardiff-reef, la-jolla-shores, la-jolla-cove, cabrillo-tidepools, border-field). Their notes now describe the boundary state rather than asserting membership. Surveyed coordinates are the only thing that moves any of them, and as of 3.1.1 they are no longer claimed to be sufficient -- the entry below states why a survey fixes the spot and not the boundary.

MPA BOUNDARIES ARE PARTLY AMBULATORY, SO A SURVEYED COORDINATE WOULD FIX THE SPOT AND NOT THE BOUNDARY. The entry above gives one reason for the 7 mpa_resolved false spots -- this file's ~100 m coordinates against a boundary within 150 m -- and that is half of it. WHAT IS EXACT: the 14 CCR 632(b) VERTICES. CDFW publishes them to three decimal minutes and they do not move; Cabrillo SMR, 632(b)(146), is five of them, the first at 32 40.600' N. lat. 117 14.820' W. long. WHAT IS NOT: the CLOSURES BETWEEN THEM. Each corridor area is 'bounded by the mean high tide line and straight lines connecting the following points in the order listed' (CDFW's own pages for Cabrillo SMR and Tijuana River Mouth SMCA, read 2026-08-01), and a mean high tide line is a water boundary. The California State Lands Commission states the rule: 'Except for those locations where the boundary has been permanently fixed by either a court or an agreement with the Commission, the boundary of most of the lands under the Commission's jurisdiction is what is referred to as an ambulatory boundary because it moves. ... This movement is because the boundary is based on the location of the water. ... As a practical matter, this means that surveys taken on separate days may show the boundary at different locations.' (slc.ca.gov/water-boundaries, read 2026-08-01). That carve-out is not theoretical -- the U.S. Supreme Court's supplemental decree of 2014-12-15 in United States v. California permanently fixed the federal/state offshore boundary -- but NOTHING IN THIS REPO RECORDS ANY SUCH FIXING FOR A SHORELINE CLOSURE IN THIS CORRIDOR. So the 150 m rule has two fixes behind it and not one: against a straight-line vertex segment a surveyed coordinate RESOLVES the spot, because both sides of the comparison are then fixed; against a mean-high-tide-line closure it NARROWS THE ERROR BAR AND CANNOT CLOSE IT, because the other side legally moves. These are shoreline areas, so the second case is the common one. This file does not record which part of which boundary each spot sits near, so this is stated about the unresolved set (moonlight-encinitas, swamis, cardiff-reef, la-jolla-shores, la-jolla-cove, cabrillo-tidepools, border-field) and not per spot. READ IT NARROWLY IN THE OTHER DIRECTION TOO: the vertices are published numbers, the areas are real, and this is not a claim that the boundary is unknown. What moves is where the water met the land on the day of the survey.

tidepool_floor_ft values are UNVERIFIED at confidence 'low' on all 8 spots. As of 1.4.0 three of them (swamis, sunset-cliffs, cabrillo-tidepools) are no longer author estimates but CEILINGS derived from observed sighting rates -- upper bounds on how permissive the floor may be, not measurements of where the reef surfaces. The other 5 remain the 1.2.0 author estimates. Sunset Cliffs and Cabrillo are still the two that most need local verification.

1.2.0 raised all 8 tidepool_floor_ft by exactly 1.5 ft. The 1.1.x values (-0.8 to -0.2) encoded EXCELLENT tidepooling, not workable tidepooling, and the difference is not cosmetic: over the 7 days from 2026-07-28, station 9410230 put 49 of the 56 grid cells in 'above-floor' -- the reef never surfaces -- and the remaining 7 in 'dark'. Not one usable window in a week, which is not what a week of San Diego tides looks like. Two independent sources put the workable threshold at about +1 ft MLLW and reserve negative tides for 'best' (tidepooling.org/learn: 'The best tidepooling happens during very low tides, typically below 1 foot'; lajollamom.com/best-san-diego-tide-pools: 'Low tide is less than 1 foot ... if you see a tide chart say -1 or lower, that's the best time to go'). The shift is a single constant applied uniformly rather than eight fresh guesses, so the author's RELATIVE ranking of the eight reefs is preserved intact and one number reverses the whole change. Band is now +0.7 to +1.3, straddling the +1 ft figure both sources give. Still confidence 'low'; still not field-checked.

SAFETY, stated in the direction that matters. The 1.2.0 shift moved every floor in the PERMISSIVE direction -- a higher floor means the stack calls a window open at higher water than it used to. 1.4.0 moved three of them back the other way: swamis +0.9 to 0.0, sunset-cliffs +0.7 to +0.25, cabrillo-tidepools +1.3 to +1.0. All three are STRICTER than what they replace, which is the direction a ceiling derived from a permissiveness rule can move in. sunset-cliffs went -0.8 to +0.7 in 1.2.0 and its own notes say a wrong floor there strands people; it is now +0.25, and it is no longer the strictest of the eight because swamis is at 0.0. Strictest-of-eight was always a ranking rather than a verification, and it still is: nobody has stood on that ledge system at any of these values and confirmed it. The 5 unchanged floors remain 1.2.0 author estimates in the permissive direction. Field-check Sunset Cliffs and Cabrillo before any of these numbers is presented as advice.
Per-spot surf threshold offsets are not yet modelled. Black's and Tourmaline are the clearest cases where a shared buoy reading means very different things.

floor_evidence is populated on all 8 tidepool spots and records that not one floor has instrumented evidence behind it. Every spot's first entry is method 'author_estimate', carrying the 1.1.1 value and the uniform +1.5 ft raise 1.2.0 applied to all 8. All 8 stay tidepool_floor_confidence 'low': the promotion rule needs two different methods agreeing within 0.3 ft with at least one instrumented, nothing in this repo is instrumented, and the inat_revealed entries are upper bounds that are explicitly barred from being one side of that comparison. As of 1.4.0 every spot carries an inat_revealed entry against shared/calibration.json 1.1.0. On the 3 that publish (swamis, sunset-cliffs, cabrillo-tidepools) it carries a value_ft and that value is now the floor in force -- a CEILING from the permissiveness rule, not an estimate. On the 5 that refuse (cardiff-reef, torrey-pines-beach, la-jolla-shores, la-jolla-cove, windansea) value_ft is null and the note says what refused, so 'no evidence gathered' can be told apart from 'evidence gathered and it refused'; none of those 5 floors moved. The earlier entries against calibration.json 1.0.0 are kept unedited because this ledger is append-only, and their per-bin counts and amplitude ratios are superseded: 1.0.0 used 6 bins and read background off a single bin, 1.1.0 uses 10 and pools the background band.

The MARINe Biodiversity Surveys site list has been checked against all 8 tidepool spots as of 1.3.1, and every spot now carries a marine_topography entry -- but not one of them carries an elevation, so the sweep changed no floor and promoted nothing. What it found: 3 spots sit on a Biodiversity Survey site (cabrillo-tidepools 70 m from 'Cabrillo I', windansea 236 m from 'Wind and Sea', sunset-cliffs 437 m from 'Sunset Cliffs'); 1 is unresolved (la-jolla-cove, where the published coordinate for 'La Jolla Caves' is 1142 m away but MARINe's prose places that site inside Matlahuayl SMR, essentially on top of this spot, and nothing public arbitrates); and 4 are not in the network at all (swamis, cardiff-reef, torrey-pines-beach, la-jolla-shores). Distances are read against a combined 1-sigma of 364 m -- this file's ~100 m coordinates and the 350 m coordinateUncertaintyInMeters the MARINe dataset carries per record -- so 70 m and 236 m are not distinguishable from zero, 437 m is the awkward middle and is deliberately NOT called same-bench, and anything past 1 km is a different reef. Two spots would have been bound to the wrong reef by name alone: MARINe's 'Cardiff Reef' is 1950 m from ours, at the south end of Cardiff State Beach by MARINe's own description, and MARINe's 'Swami's Beach' runs Long-Term Monitoring only, which has no topography component. The elevation itself is NOT PUBLISHED anywhere: the three Coastal Biodiversity Survey extracts carry coordinates, event dates and depth 0.0 and no elevation or vertical-datum field, topography is not among the assets MARINe's data-request page offers, and the datum is stated inconsistently between the survey-methods page (elevation relative to MLLW) and the Data Assets PDF of 2025-10-21 (referenced to a per-site benchmark bolt, no vertical datum named anywhere in the document). So MARINe does not remove the lidar deliverable anywhere. At 3 spots it converts that work from modelling an elevation to requesting one and pinning its datum, and THAT REQUEST HAS NOT BEEN MADE; for la-jolla-shores, cardiff-reef and torrey-pines-beach lidar remains the only instrumented route. n is null on all 8 entries because a site-list lookup has no sample count: the survey-round counts are stated in each note rather than borrowed into a field that means collapsed visits on the inat_revealed entries. All 8 stay tidepool_floor_confidence 'low'. Section 7 does list MARINe transect topography as an instrumented method, so this sweep looks like it unlocks promotion, and it does not: with value_ft null there is nothing for a second method to agree with.

1.4.0 set three tidepool_floor_ft values from the permissiveness rule declared in calibration/floor-calibration.md section 7: no floor may admit a marginal band whose observed sighting rate is below 2x that spot's own tide-independent background. swamis +0.9 to 0.0, sunset-cliffs +0.7 to +0.25, cabrillo-tidepools +1.3 to +1.0. What these values ARE: ceilings -- the most permissive floor the rule allows on a band holding at least the 15 visits a bin needs to be usable. What they are NOT: measurements of the elevation at which each bench surfaces. Nobody has surveyed any of them and the rule is silent about where the floor actually is; it only forbids values above these. Only cabrillo-tidepools has a crossing this corpus can locate exactly, on a marginal band of 30 visits. sunset-cliffs and swamis are the CONSERVATIVE END OF A BRACKET: at both, the band that would justify a higher ceiling clears the rate bar but holds fewer than 15 visits -- 14 at sunset-cliffs, one short, and 8 at swamis -- so the true ceiling lies somewhere above the value set and this corpus cannot say where. Both were resolved downward because the rule fails toward the restriction. The remaining limitation does not go away with more data of this kind: SIGHTING RATE IS NOT WALKABILITY. The gate asks whether the bench is workable; the curve measures whether somebody photographed a target species. The relationship is monotone across every usable bin at all three spots, so the SHAPE is trustworthy -- the LEVEL is an assumption, and it is the reason confidence stays 'low' and the reason the lidar deliverable is not optional. The other 5 floors are untouched; those spots refuse the method and no amount of additional citizen-science data sets a floor there.
